title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Life-Saving Health and Nutrition Services to Vulnerable Populations in Baidoa District

description.narrative: ltpgtRural areas of Baidoa District in Bay Region continue to face high levels of acute malnutrition and preventable morbidity, driven by prolonged drought, food insecurity, population displacement, and reduced access to essential health and nutrition services. According to recent IPC and FSNAU analyses, many communities remain in IPC Phase 3 and above, with children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) disproportionately affected. Service delivery gaps persist in remote villages due to limited facility coverage, funding shortfalls, and interruptions to nutrition services, including the suspension of TSFP following CSB++ stock-outs.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project aims to restore and strengthen access to integrated, life-saving health and nutrition services in Ahmed Gurey, Waaberi, Horseed, Raydabaale, October, and Dariiqa villages. Implementation will be anchored in four fixed service delivery sites and two mobile outreach sites, ensuring coverage of both settled and hard-to-reach populations. The project prioritizes children under five and PLW, while embedding protection mainstreaming, accountability, and inclusion across all components. Integrated health services will include outpatient consultations, routine immunization (measles and DPT1–3), antenatal and postnatal care, skilled birth attendance, clinical management of rape, and referral of complicated cases to Baidoa District Hospital, supported by ambulance services. Nutrition services will be fully integrated within health delivery platforms, with systematic screening for acute malnutrition conducted at OPD, EPI, ANC, PNC, mobile outreach, mass MUAC campaigns, and through Family/Mother MUAC.ltbrgtChildren identified with Severe Acute Malnutrition will be admitted and treated through Outpatient Therapeutic Programme (OTP) services, with RUTF and routine medications supplied by UNICEF through the existing Programme Document with DMO. Complicated cases will be referred to stabilization centres. To strengthen prevention and mitigate risks arising from TSFP service disruptions, the project will implement IYCF counselling, establish village-level care groups, deliver group IYCF messaging at health and nutrition sites, and conduct cooking demonstrations promoting locally appropriate foods such as Kobciye Shurbad.ltbrgtThe project will reach 22,600 individuals, based on vulnerability-based targeting already completed through community engagement and baseline assessments, prioritizing marginalized and minority-affiliated households, female-headed households, persons with disabilities, and households facing multiple protection risks. Protection mainstreaming will be reinforced through community engagement sessions, strengthened complaints and feedback mechanisms (including the SHF hotline), PSEA risk mitigation measures, and formal agreements with community leaders incorporating PSEA clauses.ltbrgtImplementation will be led by DMO, a local organization with established operational capacity in Baidoa District, in close coordination with Health and Nutrition Clusters, local authorities, and Area-Based Coordination (ABC) structures. A structured exit strategy focused on system strengthening, local capacity development, and knowledge transfer will support continuity beyond the project period. data collection, reporting and implementation will be led and governed by the Somalia National guidelines and cluster tools. ltbrgtlt/pgt
